extraction.name: TOFU
extraction.description: A benchmark for unlearning in LLMs built from 200 diverse synthetic/fictitious author profiles, each with 20 question-answer pairs, with a subset designated as the forget set for evaluating unlearning efficacy.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini; Zhili Feng; Avi Schwarzschild; Zachary C. Lipton; J. Zico Kolter
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The evaluation uses a structured framework of four specialized datasets: Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts, consisting of question-answer pairs about fictitious authors, real-world authors, and general world knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Question-answer pairs from four datasets: questions and answers about select fake authors to forget, other fictitious authors to retain, real-world authors, and general world facts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset labels/annotations were generated synthetically by GPT-4. The authors prompted GPT-4 with predefined author attributes and instructed it to generate 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author, with detailed, self-contained answers and the author's full name appearing in each question. Additional paraphrased and factually incorrect perturbed answers were also generated with GPT-4 for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports manual inspection of generated data diversity and compares word frequencies between prompting strategies to assess bias/confounders in the generated annotations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate the question-answer pairs, paraphrased answers, and factually incorrect perturbations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark covers only some unlearning scenarios: it focuses on entity-level forgetting, excludes instance-level and behavior-level unlearning, targets only evaluation of unlearning efficacy rather than identifying forget/retain sets, currently provides exact forget and retain sets a priori, and leaves out in-context unlearning.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses unlearning in relation to the Right to be Forgotten and notes that in-context unlearning does not provide real privacy protections in that sense.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Information about people/person entities is involved in the forgetting task.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is intended for researchers and practitioners to think about and evaluate unlearning methods, specifically to measure the efficacy of unlearning algorithms using provided forget and retain sets.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark may be updated in the future to add a constraint disallowing use of the original retain set.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was split into forget and retain subsets at three severity levels: 90-10, 95-5, and 99-1, corresponding to forgetting 10%, 5%, or 1% of authors.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was generated by prompting GPT-4 with predefined author attributes to create 20 question-answer pairs per fictitious author; the authors' attributes were deterministically seeded to reduce bias and confounding leakage, and book-title seed words were randomly selected from the Goodreads Books dataset to diversify outputs.

name.evidence: we present TOFU, a Task of Fictitious Unlearning, as a benchmark

description.evidence: We offer a dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, and a subset of these profiles called the forget set that serves as the target for unlearning.

creator.evidence: Pratyush Maini ... Zhili Feng ... Avi Schwarzschild ... Zachary C. Lipton ... J. Zico Kolter

inLanguage.evidence: We offer a dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The evaluation framework includes four distinct datasets: Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we use a structured approach with specialized datasets

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Examples of question answer pairs from all four datasets used in evaluating model utility and forget quality.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “we curate a unique dataset composed entirely of fictitious author biographies, synthesized by GPT-4... Using these attributes as a seed data, the model is tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author.”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “With this modification, we find that the generated data is significantly more diverse (based on manual inspection), see Figure 2.”

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: “the model is tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author.”

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: “synthesized by GPT-4” and “We generate paraphrased strings by asking GPT-4 to paraphrase the answer. We also generate a set of five perturbations Apert with GPT-4”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: “not all scenarios are covered, and there are areas of unlearning that fall outside the TOFU framework”; “the aim in all settings we consider is entity level forgetting”; “we leave this variation for future work”; “Our benchmark specifically targets the second problem—how to measure the efficacy of an unlearning algorithm (since we provide the forget sets exactly)”; “In the current benchmark, we provide a retain set”; “The purview of TOFU also leaves out in-context unlearning.”

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: “we choose to separate out the type of unlearning related to the Right to be Forgotten” and “it amounts to a form of prompt engineering and does not yield any real privacy in terms of the Right to be Forgotten.”

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: “we have a set of people about whom we want the model to forget everything” and “one might wish to forget only the answer to a specific question about a person”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: “Our benchmark is designed to help researchers and practitioners think about and evaluate unlearning methods” and “Our benchmark specifically targets the second problem—how to measure the efficacy of an unlearning algorithm (since we provide the forget sets exactly).”

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: “TOFU could be updated in the future to include a constraint not to use the original retain set”

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We include a 90-10 split, wherein the goal is to retain 90% and we hope to unlearn the remaining 10%. Additionally, we have 95-5 and 99-1 splits, as well.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: This dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on certain predefined attributes... the model is tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author... we use an elaborate prompt that deterministically seeds various author attributes... To seed names for the book titles, we use the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.
